message.content: Handlers in this codebase return a mode/data reply hash instead of a bare status string because it enables a structured, extensible response format that can carry multiple pieces of information simultaneously—such as operation status, returned data, metadata, and error details—without requiring the protocol layer to parse or interpret arbitrary string formats. This design decouples the handler implementation from the response encoding logic, allowing handlers to focus solely on business logic while the transport layer is responsible for serializing the hash into the appropriate wire format. It also future-proofs the protocol: new response fields can be added to the hash structure without breaking existing clients, and it supports richer feedback (e.g., partial results, pagination tokens, or transaction IDs) that a simple status string could never express.
